violations.why: Timer_B (equal priority) can preempt Timer_A between the increment and the check, so the check sees B's value.
Timer_C preempts Timer_A after its write and overwrites the value before the check.
Timer_Force preempts and increments, so the check reads a changed value.
Timer_Reset preempts and zeroes the counter before the check.
The increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write; Timer_B can write in between, so its update is lost.
Timer_C's write is lost when the preempted increment completes.
Timer_Force's increment is lost when the preempted increment writes back.
Timer_Reset's zeroing is overwritten by the preempted increment.
Timer_A (equal priority) can preempt Timer_B between its write and check, so the check no longer sees 1.
Timer_C can write between B's write and its check.
Timer_Force increments between B's write and check, so the check fails.
Timer_Reset zeroes the counter between B's write and check.
Timer_Reset (highest priority) preempts Timer_C between its write and check and resets the counter.
Timer_C preempts Timer_Force's read-modify-write, and its write is lost.
Timer_Reset preempts Timer_Force's increment, and the reset is overwritten.
